front: Tu connais Paul ? Oui, je le connais bien.
pronunciation: [tü koh-neh POL ? WEE, zhuh luh koh-neh BYAN]
back: Do you know Paul? Yes, I know him well.
context: Direct object pronouns (COD): le, la, les replace a person or thing directly after the verb. They go BEFORE the verb.

front: Tu as vu ma clé ? Non, je ne l'ai pas vue.
pronunciation: [tü ah vü mah KLAY ? NOHN, zhuh nuh lay pah VÜ]
back: Have you seen my key? No, I haven't seen it.
context: Le/la → l' before a vowel. In the passé composé the participle agrees with a preceding direct object: vue (la clé).

front: Les documents ? Je les ai envoyés ce matin.
pronunciation: [lay doh-kü-MAHN ? zhuh lay zay ahn-vwah-yay suh mah-TAN]
back: The documents? I sent them this morning.
context: 'Les' + agreement: envoyés.
Me, te, nous, vous work as both direct and indirect pronouns.

front: Tu as parlé à ta mère ? Oui, je lui ai parlé hier.
pronunciation: [tü ah par-lay ah tah MEHR ? WEE, zhuh lwee ay par-lay YEHR]
back: Did you talk to your mother? Yes, I talked to her yesterday.
context: Indirect object pronouns (COI): lui (him/her), leur (them) replace 'à + person'.

front: Je leur ai offert des fleurs.
context: 'Leur' (to them) never takes an s. Don't confuse it with the possessive 'leurs'.
'Manquer à' takes an indirect object: il me manque = I miss him.

front: Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'y vais demain.
pronunciation: [tü vah ah pah-REE ? WEE, zhee veh duh-MAN]
back: Are you going to Paris? Yes, I'm going there tomorrow.
context: 'Y' replaces a place introduced by à, en, dans, chez…: there.
'Y' also replaces 'à + thing': penser à ce voyage → y penser.

front: Tu as besoin d'aide ? Non, je n'en ai pas besoin.
pronunciation: [tü ah buh-zwan DED ? NOHN, zhuh nahn nay pah buh-ZWAN]
back: Do you need help? No, I don't need it.
context: 'En' replaces 'de + thing': avoir besoin de → en avoir besoin.

front: Tu veux du café ? Oui, j'en veux bien.
pronunciation: [tü vuh dü kah-FAY ? WEE, zhahn vuh BYAN]
back: Do you want some coffee? Yes, I'd like some.
context: 'En' replaces du/de la/des + noun: some, any.

front: Combien de frères as-tu ? J'en ai deux.
pronunciation: [kohm-byan duh FREHR ah-TÜ ? zhahn nay DUH]
back: How many brothers do you have? I have two.
context: With numbers and quantities, 'en' is required: j'en ai deux (never 'j'ai deux').

back: There are a lot of them.
context: 'Il y en a' = there are some.

front: Des pommes ? J'en ai acheté un kilo.
pronunciation: [day PUM ? zhahn nay ahsh-tay an kee-LOH]
back: Apples? I bought a kilo (of them).
context: 'En' + quantity: j'en ai acheté un kilo. The participle does NOT agree with 'en'.
Pronoun order: me/te/nous/vous BEFORE le/la/les.
Order: le/la/les BEFORE lui/leur.

back: I talked to him about it.
context: 'En' always comes last: lui en, leur en, m'en.
'Y' comes before 'en': il y en a.
In the affirmative imperative, pronouns go after the verb: le/la before moi/lui.
In the negative imperative, the normal order comes back.
'Y' with the imperative of aller; the s returns for the liaison.
'En' after the imperative: prends-en, manges-en (the s returns before en).

back: I'm going to call him tomorrow.
context: With two verbs, the pronoun goes before the infinitive: je vais LE voir.

front: Je ne peux pas y aller ce soir.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh puh pah zee ah-lay suh SWAHR]
context: Pronoun before the infinitive.
'Se souvenir de' → s'en souvenir.
'S'occuper de' → s'en occuper.
Informal. Stronger: 'je m'en fous' (vulgar).

back: That doesn't stop you from doing it.
context: 'Empêcher quelqu'un de' → l'en empêcher.
Combination le/la/les + y.

front: Ce livre ? Je l'ai trouvé passionnant.
back: This book? I found it gripping.
context: Topic first, then the pronoun: very natural in spoken French.

front: Qu'est-ce que tu leur as dit ?
context: 'Leur' = to them.

front: Elle nous a invités à son mariage.
pronunciation: [el noo zah an-vee-tay ah sohn mah-RYAZH]
back: She invited us to her wedding.
context: 'Nous' as a direct object: the participle agrees (invités).

back: Shall we talk about it tomorrow?
context: 'Parler de' → en parler.
'Arriver à faire quelque chose' → y arriver = to manage.
'En vouloir à quelqu'un' = to be angry with someone. 'Je ne t'en veux pas' = I'm not angry with you.
